messages:
ops-bot: PagerDuty INC-2026-9984 triggered: elevated 5xx + timeouts observed from canary namespace (us-west2). Alerting oncall and eng-sre.

sophie: seeing the same on dashboards — p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~ 2.8s, 5xx rate ~ 6% on canary. Affects ~10% of traffic to /generate.

miguel: @sophie can you paste the canary deployment id?

sophie: deploy id: canary-v2026-1117 (rolled at 2135999800).

alex: oncall handoff: i'm oncall-sre for the next 2h. i'll take lead. @miguel @kai please join.

oncall-sre: copying metrics, traces. Top-level symptom: client-level timeouts (gateway) and transient 5xx from runtime. Latency tail spikes align with longer KV cache miss windows.

kai: stack traces show backend service returning 504 from router pool when forwarding to runtime pods. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T21:45:06Z router: forward request id=abcd1234 -> runtime-3 timeout after 1500ms
runtime-3: warn: kvcache miss, refill 2.1s
```

miguel: curious — did canary enable any new batching or multiplex config?

sophie: yes, canary toggled "adaptive_prefetch": true and increased default batch_size to 64.

alex: that rings a bell. adaptive_prefetch seems to cause more KV cache churn if model shard layout changes. onload of new canary pods may thrash the prefix cache.

oncall-sre: customer impact: internal telemetry shows 18 external customers hit intermittent timeouts; top affected routes are conversational generate and streaming. CS flagged two paying customers with dropped requests.

cs-lead: we started receiving customer tickets. Notifying affected accounts now, telling them we're investigating and may roll back.

kai: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable canary routing, 2) rollback canary to previous model, 3) tweak routing timeout/fallback to faster variant. I recommend rollback to previous canary if impact persists.

miguel: we can also flip adaptive_prefetch=false via feature-flag config without a full deploy — that's lower blast radius.

alex: can we toggle the flag for the canary group only?

sophie: yes, config is done per deployment group. issuing command now: `/feature-flag set canary-v2026-1117 adaptive_prefetch false`

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Applying flag to canary-v2026-1117...

deploy-bot: Applied feature-flag update to 3 pods in canary-v2026-1117 (started 2136004502).

kai: monitoring... p95 dropping from 1.2s -> 400ms within 30s. p99 still at 1.1s. 5xx rate down to 2.3%.

oncall-sre: good improvement but still above baseline. Do we want a rollback?

miguel: i vote rollback. adaptive_prefetch off helped but p99 still high and we risk more customer tickets. rollback will restore previous batch_size and other defaults.

alex: initiating rollback to stable-v2026-1109. Rolling back canary group only, will stop new canary traffic. Command: `/deploy rollback canary-v2026-1117 to stable-v2026-1109 --reason "p99/timeouts"`

deploy-bot: Rollback started: stopping canary traffic and deploying stable-v2026-1109 to canary pins. Progress: pod 1/3 updated at 2136004920, pod 2/3 updated at 2136004985, pod 3/3 updated at 2136005050.

ops-bot: Incident note: rolling back canary-v2026-1117 — reason: timeout/p99 regression. Pager duty incident status -> acknowledged.

sophie: after full rollback, p95 ~ 140ms, p99 ~ 210ms, 5xx < 0.2%. Looks back to baseline within 90s of final pod update.

cs-lead: sending follow-up message to impacted customers: "We've rolled back a recent canary due to elevated timeouts and 5xx; service performance restored. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

miguel: collecting traces for root cause. hypothesis: adaptive_prefetch + larger batch_size increased cold KV cache refills frequency, causing long tail on first requests to shards. Also possible kernel scheduling due to increased batch costs.

kai: pulled hot traces; pattern: sequence lengths small but batching induced bigger compute windows leading to more long-running kernels and router timeouts. We'll add more instrumentation around KV cache hit/miss latencies and kernel durations.

alex: next steps: 1) create a postmortem draft, 2) add a regression test in canary pipeline to toggle adaptive_prefetch and measure p99 under representative traffic, 3) consider a graceful backoff in router instead of hard 1500ms timeouts.

oncall-sre: setting incident status -> resolved (service restored). keeping thread open for postmortem notes.

ops-bot: Incident closed at 2136006121. Tags: rollback, p99-regression, canary, kvcache, feature-flag.

sophie: quick note for postmortem: include customer impact list, exact timing of feature-flag flip and rollback, and logs from runtime-*. Also consider safe defaults for new canary toggles.

miguel: i'll own postmortem. creating doc and linking here when ready.

alex: thanks everyone for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
